assessment: All 15 retained main-PDF pages were read as text and visually inspected, with eight magnifications. Ten numbered figures plus the graphical abstract, three tables, all main sections and 63 printed references were inspected. The main PDF has no formal numbered equations; mathematical realizations are deferred to unverified SM1. The 57 limited checks and disclosed geometry, nonuniqueness and shared-sink examples do not reproduce native ITEAM, GIS, cost or physical models. Two original-passage edges support bounded context; 61 other originals and 14 dependencies or scope requirements remain open. No accepted Paper 1 input was added.

claims.claim: CCUS can contribute to decarbonizing fossil-intensive industry and energy.
claims.assessment: Context references, rather than a complete lifecycle or facility inventory in this paper.

claims.claim: Deep saline aquifers contribute over 90% of storage potential but have sparse data and heterogeneous trapping behavior.
claims.assessment: Resource context and geological uncertainty do not establish annual pressure-limited service or verified retention.

claims.claim: China has spatial source–sink mismatch, with transport/storage costs above 60 USD/t in some cases.
claims.assessment: Historical cost/geographic context; not a universal cost or current contracted service.

claims.claim: Several Chinese onshore and offshore basins have been assessed with inconsistent data and methods.
claims.assessment: Six supporting regional originals remain unverified; no exhaustive national literature audit is reproduced.

claims.claim: Existing models poorly integrate capacity, economics, matching and policy, limiting national analysis.
claims.assessment: Scoped Lin original passages support four broad challenges, rather than proof that every prior model lacks integration.

claims.claim: Storage assessment has theoretical, effective, practical and matched tiers across basin, zone and site scales.
claims.assessment: Hierarchical terms need their native algorithms; a tier is not a calibrated annual injection bound.

claims.claim: Offshore assessments often focus on individual basins or theoretical basin-scale capacity.
claims.assessment: Originals and the scope of this literature claim remain unverified.

claims.claim: ITEAM-CCS hub integrates national sources, geology, suitability, capacity, costs, matching and pipeline generation at 1 km resolution.
claims.assessment: Software integration is described, but no native implementation, data or accuracy benchmark is reproduced.

claims.claim: The zone framework complements Petrel, TOUGH2 and MRST by supporting national planning.
claims.assessment: Complementary scope, rather than greater physical accuracy or an independently validated substitute for field models.

claims.claim: Onshore and offshore suitability and economic models are assessed separately.
claims.assessment: Their index definitions, scales and comparability require the supporting material.

claims.claim: The results serve macro-assessment and preliminary feasibility and cannot underpin site screening or project design.
claims.assessment: Explicit source limitation retained in Paper 1; no source-site licensing or safe operating envelope inferred.

claims.claim: Large-scale schemes can combine near mass balance, injection and geofluid-production wells, multiple strata and risk mitigation.
claims.assessment: Hypothesized engineering strategy, not supplied water volumes, pumping/disposal utilities or verified pressure limits.

claims.claim: Suitability combines storage performance, safety/risk and social-economic/environmental constraints.
claims.assessment: Weights, normalization and on/offshore criteria in S2/S3 remain unverified; categories are not failure probabilities.

claims.claim: Capacity methods include empirical, analytical, reduced-order, numerical, AI and hybrid approaches selected by data quality.
claims.assessment: The mathematical realizations are deferred to SM1; no formal numbered equation appears in the main PDF.

claims.claim: Source screening uses enterprise location, process, output, fuels, water, electricity and emission quantities/concentrations.
claims.assessment: Naming data does not supply a complete matched capture/conditioning utility balance; facility records remain unavailable locally.

claims.claim: Source-screening criteria vary by industry and region, with P10/P90 details referred to capacity algorithms in the supplement.
claims.assessment: The apparent section cross-reference does not supply a quantile definition or original algorithm.

claims.claim: Storage costs depend on site performance, platforms, wells, injection strategies and parameters; all money is escalated to 2022 USD.
claims.assessment: Original cost models are cited; a scoped SimCCS check supports economic/geospatial precedent, not China case validation. Escalation indices and native parameters are missing.

claims.claim: P2P and M2M pairing use pipeline routes and cost surfaces within search radii.
claims.assessment: The main PDF gives no formal objective, network constraints or native optimization cases; candidate radius is not necessarily actual pipe length.

claims.claim: All modeled sources promptly retrofit and operate at their assumed capacities.
claims.assessment: Explicit simultaneous deployment assumption; proposed policy stages are not a native annual construction/dispatch schedule.

claims.claim: Subsurface data span basin, regional and site scales; surface data include geology, terrain, networks, climate and social-economic layers.
claims.assessment: Taxonomy and multi-resolution integration do not establish every layer's accuracy; originals and S13 remain unverified.

claims.claim: Institutional geological sources and petroleum/project parameters support the data compilation.
claims.assessment: Exact versions and access are pending. The cited 1994–2009 US equipment-cost lineage needs transparent 2022 escalation and regional transfer.

claims.claim: Table 1 associates one well per 25/100/400/2500 km² with spacing below 5/10/20/50 km.
claims.assessment: Square-root arithmetic agrees with boundary values, but does not prove equivalence for irregular well patterns; preserve strict inequalities and printed map scales.

claims.claim: Data fusion creates about 1 km × 1 km or 0.01° × 0.01° grids.
claims.assessment: Angular area changes with latitude; native CRS, cell areas, resampling and aggregation weights are required. No erroneous source area is assumed.

claims.claim: The 1 km grid is interpolated from well spacing of 20–50 km and cannot resolve unobserved small faults, channels or barriers.
claims.assessment: Explicit source limitation: output cell size is not observation density or predictive accuracy. Denser wells/seismic data are needed for site claims.

claims.claim: Four-sector 2022 emissions total 8.9 Gt, with 4,673 source records and 226 Mt/y high-concentration CO₂.
claims.assessment: Counts close; the literal emission rows sum to 8,914.2 versus 8,914.1 Mt/y, compatible with displayed rounding. Do not add the 226 Mt/y again without its native membership.

claims.claim: At 85% net capture, about 7.6 Gt/y could be captured.
claims.assessment: 8,914.1 × 0.85 = 7,576.985 Mt/y. Capture is distinct from full-chain avoidance, injection and permanent retention. Feed vol% is also distinct from capture efficiency.

claims.claim: Captive-power double counting is possible; 320 Mt/y and excluded small sources are described as negligible against 4.34 Gt/y coal power.
claims.assessment: 320/4,658.2 is about 6.87%. Removing 320 conditionally reconstructs 4.3382 Gt/y but is not an accepted deduplication or a justified negligible-error criterion.

claims.claim: Basins have different tectonics, reservoir/seal properties, porosity, permeability and sediment thickness.
claims.assessment: Regional ranges are not site-specific pressure/risk calibration. Central 5–15% and 0.1–10 mD, western 12–20% and 10 km, and offshore 8 km are retained as source context.

claims.claim: Several offshore basins have high suitability, capacity, injectivity and safety, with typical costs below 10/30 USD/t on/offshore.
claims.assessment: Qualitative regional rankings, not measured safety or universal bounds; later cost ranges and map outliers require case scope.

claims.claim: Theoretical and effective capacity totals are about 2.5 and 1.5 trillion tonnes.
claims.assessment: Table 3 sums close exactly at displayed precision. These are resource stocks, rather than annual physical service.

claims.claim: Capacity density spans 0.01–1.35 Mt/km²; large basin areas and strata support substantial resources.
claims.assessment: Figure 6 legend includes zero; neither a colour nor a nominal 1 km pixel supplies a precise stock without original area/mask data.

claims.claim: Theoretical P10–P90 spans 1.25–3.76 trillion tonnes, while matched capacity is 4.2–6.1 Gt/y across 150–800 km.
claims.assessment: Only capacity ranges are supplied; quantile convention, joint uncertainty and native pressure constraints remain unverified.

claims.claim: P50 onshore/offshore theoretical stocks are 1305.7/1201.6 Gt, and effective stocks 756.2/743.6 Gt.
claims.assessment: Nearly balanced stocks do not imply balanced annual matched flows; onshore provides roughly 89–91% of the matched totals.

claims.claim: Most offshore storage costs are 10–60 USD/t, compared with 3–10 onshore.
claims.assessment: 2022-USD regional ranges, not universal minima/maxima; Figure 7 includes >100 USD/t and a None category that is not zero.

claims.claim: High-pressure buildup can limit capacity and increase risk, requiring well-field and water-recovery design.
claims.assessment: Acknowledges the mechanism but supplies no validated annual maximum rates, pressure controls or water-treatment inventory.

claims.claim: Over 99% of sources have suitable onshore or offshore candidates within 800 km.
claims.assessment: Source-count geographical eligibility differs from mass served, economic deployment and shared-sink feasibility.

claims.claim: At costs below 90 USD/t, 85% capture yields 4.2 Gt/y at 150 km and 6.0 Gt/y at 800 km, described as 59–79% of captured emissions.
claims.assessment: 4.2/7.6 is 55.26%, while 6.0/7.6 is 78.95%. Conditional display intervals cannot explain 59%; preserve the unresolved denominator or case distinction.

claims.claim: Avoidance costs exceed levelized costs because CCS uses energy and creates emissions.
claims.assessment: The native capture, avoided-mass and project-emission arrays are missing; exact full-chain duties cannot be recovered from the plotted difference.

claims.claim: Plateaus reflect onshore/offshore transitions and basin heterogeneity; beyond about 300 km transport dominates costs.
claims.assessment: Source interpretation, not an independently reproduced causal or sensitivity result; route, land and infrastructure arrays are needed.

claims.claim: Urban, water, rail and conservation costs motivate backbone pipelines and clusters.
claims.assessment: Policy/economic implication, rather than validated shared-network savings under the native M2M model.

claims.claim: Over 69% of captured CO₂ costs 30–60 USD/t and over 79% of cases cost less than 90 USD/t.
claims.assessment: Mass shares, project counts, radius scenarios and denominators must be separated; do not merge this with abstract 60–75% or implications 64–75%.

claims.claim: P50 suitability, capacities and costs are consistent with Ordos, Yulin, Enping and Bohai Bay project assessments.
claims.assessment: No native comparisons, tolerances or held-out case definition are printed; the authors' consistency statement is not an independently reproduced validation.

claims.claim: Basin cost curves have smooth or stepwise features due to source distribution, storage zones and matching.
claims.assessment: Figure 9 uses a logarithmic mass axis and Levelized Cost ordinate despite its abatement-cost caption. Exact curve arrays and category partitions remain open.

claims.claim: Provincial curves differ between centralized single-basin and multibasin regions.
claims.assessment: Figure 10 has 34 native region labels and a linear mass axis. Native names are preserved as geography; plotted limits do not establish terminal capacities.

claims.claim: Regional geology, land/energy costs and source characteristics explain sectoral and administrative cost differences.
claims.assessment: Qualitative attribution requires native sensitivity/counterfactual cases. No complete utility inventory follows from CO₂-concentration categories.

claims.claim: Coastal marine basins can halve abatement costs through proximal pairing.
claims.assessment: The exact comparator, cases and common avoided-mass/cost boundary are not supplied.

claims.claim: Twelve coalitions and carbon corridors are proposed, including integrated land/sea basins.
claims.assessment: Named proposals are not implemented agreements, infrastructure or field-service contracts; duplicate/overlapping basin partitions need native mapping.

claims.claim: Enterprise sharing, provincial agreements and statutory corridors can enable cost, technical and policy synergy and industrial relocation.
claims.assessment: A proposed roadmap, not a native multi-period schedule or independent prediction of jobs, economic revival or deployment.

claims.claim: China has a cost advantage versus the US, Central Asia and Europe and can reduce stranded-asset risk.
claims.assessment: Cross-study costs need common currency year, scope, capacity, technology and denominator; no matched international comparison was reproduced.

claims.claim: Uncertainty analysis is constrained by input ranges and computational cost; matching relies on P50 medians.
claims.assessment: Explicit limitation; P50 is not a probability of project success or evidence of calibrated joint uncertainty.

claims.claim: The analysis focuses on saline aquifers and excludes oilfield content, even though EOR profit/pricing is discussed.
claims.assessment: Do not pool illustrative utilization/oilfield schematics with the quantitative saline-aquifer cost boundary.

claims.claim: CCS alone cannot deliver 100% net mitigation for coal-based industry; complementary energy/removal options are needed.
claims.assessment: Residual emissions are acknowledged; complete counterfactual and retained-carbon accounting remains outside the supplied numerical evidence.

claims.claim: Implications say 64–75% of industrial emissions can be stored within 300 km below 90 USD/t.
claims.assessment: For the same Table 2/3 case, all 300 km matches are only 61.36% of gross emissions or 72.18% of calculated captured emissions, before cost filtering. Case/denominator mapping is unresolved.

claims.claim: The framework could manage about 80% of coal-sector emissions and offers Global South replication.
claims.assessment: The 800 km total is about 80.6% of calculated captured mass but 68.5% of gross Table 2 emissions. Do not silently choose a denominator or treat transfer as field validation.

claims.claim: The database covers 16 onshore basins and 15 offshore areas with 1 km analysis and 12 coalition candidates.
claims.assessment: 31 assessment areas are not 31 independently validated storage sites or safe annual operating envelopes.

claims.claim: The framework resolves spatial-temporal 5W2H planning and aligns geology, costs and policy.
claims.assessment: The prompt retrofit assumption is not a dynamic construction, dispatch or reservoir-feedback model. Transfer requires local data and transparent constraints.

claims.claim: Supporting data can be requested from the corresponding author; SM1 is linked as a free PDF.
claims.assessment: No author was contacted and no external download resumed. Native files, code and complete supporting algorithms remain unverified locally.

claims.claim: Eight authors, no competing financial interest and named Chinese/US-China funding are disclosed.
claims.assessment: Provenance only; authorship, funding and declarations neither validate results nor establish misconduct.

claims.claim: All 63 printed references support the paper's context and methods.
claims.assessment: Native bibliography read and preserved, with R19 column continuation. Two selected-original edges support bounded context; 61 originals and further literature chains remain unverified.

claims.claim: Paper 1 implication: a high-resolution national resource/matching framework does not supply field-level annual service.
claims.assessment: No pressure, injectivity, water utility or retention factor is accepted from this paper.

claims.claim: Paper 1 implication: source-count eligibility, captured/avoided mass, capacity stock and annual flow require separate denominators.
claims.assessment: 57 diagnostics and synthetic geometry/grid/LP examples do not reproduce native ITEAM, source records, cost curves or physical models.

claims.claim: Paper 1 implication: existing economic/geospatial integration and coalition proposals qualify novelty claims.
claims.assessment: Recognize the prior framework while keeping its limited native-data/model verification explicit.
